import plotly.graph_objects as go
import polars as pl


def split_chart(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, go.Figure]:
    """How many rows each side of the split holds."""
    total = train.height + test.height
    sides = ["train", "test"]
    rows = [train.height, test.height]
    figure = go.Figure(
        go.Bar(
            x=sides,
            y=rows,
            text=[f"{n:,} rows · {n / total:.0%}" for n in rows],
            textposition="outside",
        ),
        layout={"title": {"text": "Rows in train and test"}, "showlegend": False},
    )
    figure.update_yaxes(title="rows")
    return {"figure": figure}


figure = split_chart(train, test)['figure']
figure

import polars as pl
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from concepts import Target
from sprisk import operator
from validation.row_overlap import no_row_in_both
from validation.settings import Seed, TestFraction


@operator(role="split", folds="plain", promises=[no_row_in_both])
def stratified_split(
    data: pl.DataFrame, stratify: Target, test_fraction: TestFraction = 0.2, seed: Seed = 42
) -> dict[str, pl.DataFrame]:
    """Shuffle rows into train and test, keeping each class's share on both sides."""
    classes = data[stratify]
    if classes.null_count():
        raise ValueError(f"{stratify} has {classes.null_count()} missing values; drop them first")
    train_rows, test_rows = train_test_split(
        list(range(data.height)),
        test_size=test_fraction,
        random_state=seed,
        stratify=classes.to_list(),
    )
    train, test = data[sorted(train_rows)], data[sorted(test_rows)]
    if train.is_empty() or test.is_empty():
        raise ValueError(f"split gave {train.height} train and {test.height} test rows")
    return {"train": train, "test": test}

import plotly.graph_objects as go
import polars as pl

from sprisk import operator


@operator(role="chart", capability_class="analyzer")
def split_chart(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, go.Figure]:
    """How many rows each side of the split holds."""
    total = train.height + test.height
    sides = ["train", "test"]
    rows = [train.height, test.height]
    figure = go.Figure(
        go.Bar(
            x=sides,
            y=rows,
            text=[f"{n:,} rows · {n / total:.0%}" for n in rows],
            textposition="outside",
        ),
        layout={"title": {"text": "Rows in train and test"}, "showlegend": False},
    )
    figure.update_yaxes(title="rows")
    return {"figure": figure}

"""Settings the splits share, with the range a person may set."""

from typing import Annotated

from sprisk import Between

TestFraction = Annotated[float, Between(0.05, 0.40, step=0.05)]
Seed = Annotated[int, Between(0, 10000)]

"""Meanings the packs ask for. A project binds each one to a real column; column names never
appear in a pack (ADR-0063)."""

from typing import Annotated, Literal

from sprisk import Concept

ItemIdentity = Annotated[
    str,
    Concept(
        "common.item_identity",
        "entity_identifier",
        "Groups rows that describe the same real-world item.",
    ),
]
EventTime = Annotated[
    str, Concept("common.event_time", "time", "When the event a row describes happened.")
]
Target = Annotated[str, Concept("common.target", "label", "The value the model learns to predict.")]
Task = Literal["classification", "regression"]

id: methodology.supervised.split_method@1.0.0

name: Train/test split
activity: Fair evaluation
question: How are rows divided into training and test so the score is fair?
applies_when:
  task:
  - classification
  - regression

  - common.event_time
  - common.item_identity
  - common.target
  evidence: []
  decisions:
  - data.repeated_items
options:
- id: temporal
  label: Temporal split
  action:
    replace:
      role: split
      operator: sprisk.validation.temporal_split@1.0.0
      concepts:
        time_column: common.event_time
        group_column: common.item_identity
      settings:
        test_fraction: 0.2
  verify:
  - test_after_train
- id: item_groups
  label: Group split
  action:
    replace:
      role: split
      operator: sprisk.validation.group_split@1.0.0
      concepts:
        group_column: common.item_identity
      settings:
        test_fraction: 0.2
        seed: 42
  verify:
  - no_group_overlap
- id: stratified_random
  label: Stratified split
  action:
    replace:
      role: split
      operator: sprisk.validation.stratified_split@1.0.0
      concepts:
        stratify: common.target
      settings:
        test_fraction: 0.2
        seed: 42
  verify:
  - no_row_in_both
- id: simple_random
  label: Random split
  action:
    replace:
      role: split
      operator: sprisk.validation.random_split@1.0.0
      settings:
        test_fraction: 0.2
        seed: 42
  verify:
  - no_row_in_both
verifications:
  test_after_train:
    needs: evaluation.time_order
    promise: Every test row is later than the latest train row.
  no_group_overlap:
    needs: evaluation.group_overlap
    promise: No item has rows in both train and test.
  no_row_in_both:
    needs: evaluation.row_overlap
    promise: No test row has the same features as a train row.
source: "Roberts et al. (2017), Ecography 40(8): cross-validation for temporal and grouped data; scikit-learn\
  \ User Guide \xA73.1: GroupShuffleSplit, train_test_split(stratify=y)."
